candidate_relations.label: Dropped head syndrome
candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is a two-part composite: Dropped Head Syndrome as the clinical syndrome AND Isolated Neck Extensor Myopathy as the specific etiology. C001 captures the syndrome component but does not specify INEM, leaving the etiology unresolved.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Names the syndrome but omits the specific etiology (Isolated Neck Extensor Myopathy / INEM) required by the benchmark composite

candidate_relations.label: Camptocormia
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes head and neck flexion deformity (cervical spine), not trunk flexion. Camptocormia involves the thoracolumbar spine and is a differential/related condition rather than the diagnosis in this case.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Camptocormia is an axial flexion deformity of the trunk, not the neck/head; it is a related but anatomically distinct entity sometimes co-occurring with DHS

candidate_relations.label: Cervical Spondylosis
candidate_relations.reason: The benchmark diagnosis is a myopathic etiology (INEM) causing DHS. Cervical spondylosis implies degenerative bony/disc pathology as the primary diagnosis, which conflicts with the neuromuscular/myopathic etiology specified in the reference.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Cervical spondylosis is a degenerative disc/joint disease, not a myopathy causing dropped head; the mechanism and diagnostic category are incompatible

case_quality_flags: Benchmark requires both syndrome label and specific etiology (INEM); no EMG, muscle biopsy, or MRI muscle findings documented in the record to confirm INEM definitively
Dementia in history raises possibility of other neurodegenerative causes of DHS not fully excluded
